title: Portage, Indiana: the gravestones found under a gas station dig in 1962 (the Crisman stones)

factcheck.result: lines 1-6 supported (line 6 from the July 19, 1962 article alone; the second death in 1876 from the 1962 article, the first from the Dec. 7, 1876 Vidette); line 7 changed: it was the granddaughter, Mrs. Nealon, who told the paper it was still unsolved, not the paper itself; the last label changed from STILL A MYSTERY to A MYSTERY IN 1962 (nothing shows it is unsolved today); beat 5 credit now July 11 and 19 (the granddaughter is named in July 11); the sister is not named because sources spell her Marta, Martha, Myrta and Myrtie; the highway drawn without a centre line because the 1962 lane count is not known. The standard ending was kept (Scoop's rule).

sources.what: 'Grave Question' (July 11, 1962): descendants of Portage pioneers Isaac and Jane Crisman mulling over recently unearthed family gravestones; three stones, a family monument and two headstones, found by workmen excavating for a new filling station at the southeast corner of U.S. 20 and Crisman road; headstones bear the names Wilbur and Marta; the monument apparently erected by Isaac and Jane Crisman in memory of two children; 'Both the monument and headstones are of unpolished marble'; the children died in 1876 of scarlet fever, aged five and three; Isaac and Jane were the grandparents of Celia Nealon and Mrs. Max Wheat
sources.who: Vidette-Messenger (Valparaiso), July 11, 1962, vol. 36 no. 6, by Rollie Bernhart; transcribed by inportercounty.org (Crisman Cemetery)

sources.what: 'Explanation Offered Crisman Grave Mystery' (July 19, 1962): 'Any possibilities of the existence of the pioneer Crisman family cemetery at the southeast corner of U. S. 20 and Crisman road in Portage, were dissipated in a report from Mrs. Celia (Crisman) Nealon'; workmen unearthed the stones two weeks earlier; Mrs. Blair took Mrs. Nealon to a spot north of U.S. 20, the township cemetery, on a high bank overgrown with trees and thick brush, with no visible stones or markers; how the stones came to be buried at Crisman road and U.S. 20 'still remains unsolved'
sources.who: Vidette-Messenger, July 19, 1962, vol. 36 no. 13, by Rollie Bernhart; same transcription

sources.what: 'While excavating for a service station at the SE corner of US 20 in section 1, stones were found'; one stone bore the initials of I. and J. Crisman, another the names of Wilbur and Martha, children of I. and J. Crisman; Isaac Crisman married Jane White in December 1870
sources.who: Northwest Indiana Genealogical Society, Portage Township cemetery index (1995), quoted on the same page

sources.what: 'One of Ike Crisman's little children died Thursday of scarlet fever; the other is at the point of death' (Joy's Run Items)
sources.who: Porter County Vidette, Dec. 7, 1876, vol. 20 no. 49, p. 3; transcribed by inportercounty.org

sources.what: the village of Crisman was laid out by B. G. Crisman, 'after whom it was named'; Isaac Crisman its first postmaster and storekeeper
sources.who: Goodspeed and Blanchard, Counties of Porter and Lake (1882), ch. XII, Portage Township; transcribed by inportercounty.org

sources.what: Benjamin G. Crisman came to Porter County in 1850 with his family, Isaac among them; Crisman (now part of Portage) was named after him
sources.who: Ray Crisman, in A Biographical History of Porter County (1976); transcribed by inportercounty.org

beats.text: A gas station dig in Portage turned up gravestones.
beats.label: PORTAGE, INDIANA
beats.credit: History: Vidette-Messenger (1962); NW Indiana Genealogical Society

beats.text: It was July 1962. Workmen found them at the corner of US 20 and Crisman Road.
beats.label: JULY 1962

beats.text: There was a family monument and two marble headstones, for two children of pioneers Isaac and Jane Crisman.
beats.label: THE STONES

beats.text: In 1876, scarlet fever took them both, Wilbur and his sister.
But a Crisman granddaughter said the family cemetery was never at that corner.
beats.label: THE FAMILY

beats.text: She was shown the old township cemetery, north of the highway, on a bank overgrown with trees, with no stones showing.
beats.label: NORTH OF U.S. 20

beats.text: How the stones came to be buried at that corner, she told the paper, was still unsolved.
beats.label: A MYSTERY IN 1962

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.
